 Getty GOAL 17 Nov 2026 18:44-08:00 Generated by USMNT player ratings vs. Haiti: Weston McKennie pulls the strings and Christian Pulisic's impressive run continues
 Match Player ratings USA vs Haiti USA Haiti CONCACAF Nations League M. Pochettino C. Pulisic J. Hall Weston McKennie set up both goals in the 2-0 win, including Julian Hall’s fifth in six caps. The USMNT reached the Nations League semifinals 8-0 on aggregate.
 The last time the USMNT played in Cincinnati, U.S. Soccer announced Mauricio Pochettino as its new head coach. A little more than two years later, the team was back at TQL Stadium for his farewell. Twenty-five minutes in, Christian Pulisic was in the air with his back to goal. 
 Pulisic had started the move himself, carrying the ball down the left before playing it inside to Julian Hall. Hall found Weston McKennie, who floated a cross back toward Pulisic. He twisted in the air and sent his bicycle kick in off the post. The crowd got to its feet.
 Just before halftime, McKennie spotted Hall breaking behind Haiti’s back line and dropped the ball into his path. Hall took it in stride and finished with the outside of his boot. He was 16 when Pochettino got the job. He’s 18 now, with five goals in six senior appearances.
 The U.S. won 2-0 to reach March’s Concacaf Nations League semifinals 8-0 on aggregate. Pochettino heads to Manchester United after one last win shaped by two players who were already central to the team when he arrived, and a teenager who’s making a case to lead the line for whoever comes next.
 GOAL rates the USMNT's players from TQL Stadium...
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images Goalkeeper & Defense
 Diego Kochen (7/10) 
 Tested early by Dominique Simon and finished with two saves. A quiet night overall, and a second clean sheet against Haiti in four days. 
 Antonee Robinson (7/10) 
 Gave the U.S. a regular outlet on the left, pushing forward when Pulisic came inside. Made way for Baker-Whiting in the 81st minute.
 Alex Freeman (6/10) 
 A steady 90 minutes at right back. Kept the ball moving on McKennie’s side and dealt comfortably with what came his way.
 Chris Richards (6/10) 
 Had a relatively quiet first half alongside Trusty. Haiti managed just one shot on target before the break, when Neil Pierre replaced him. 
 Auston Trusty (6/10) 
 Managed the early booking well and helped keep Haiti out alongside two different center-back partners. Stayed on when Pierre replaced Richards at halftime.
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images Midfield
 Sebastian Berhalter (5/10) 
 Took several U.S. corners and had a couple of attempts himself. His 72nd-minute booking was his second of the tie and will cost him a place in March’s semifinal. 
 Tyler Adams (7/10) 
 Kept the ball moving alongside Berhalter and broke up play when Haiti tried to get out. That gave McKennie and Tillman room to work higher up the field.
 Weston McKennie (9/10) 
 The best player on the pitch. Floated a cross toward the back post for Pulisic, then spotted Hall’s run and dropped a pass over Haiti’s back line for the second. 
 Malik Tillman (7/10) 
 Found space between the lines and put a first-half effort on target. Picked up a yellow card on the hour before Balogun replaced him five minutes later. 
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images Attack
 Christian Pulisic (8/10) 
 Started the move down the left and finished it himself, adjusting to McKennie’s looping cross to send a bicycle kick in off the post. His third goal of the tie was the pick of the bunch. 
 Julian Hall (8/10) 
 Helped build the opener, then timed his run behind Haiti’s defense and finished with the outside of his boot. The 18-year-old now has five goals in six senior appearances.

 Neil Pierre (6/10) 
 Took over from Richards at halftime and settled in alongside Trusty to see out the clean sheet.
 Folarin Balogun (6/10) 
 Replaced Tillman in the 65th minute and had little sight of goal as the game slowed.
 Cavan Sullivan (5/10) 
 Booked for entering the field without permission as he came on for Pulisic. Struggled to make much of an impact from the left. 
 Santiago Castañeda (6/10) 
 Made his senior debut in the 77th minute in place of McKennie and kept things simple as the U.S. closed out the win. 
 Reed Baker-Whiting (N/A) 
 Made his senior debut at left back, replacing Robinson in the 81st minute. 
 Mauricio Pochettino (8/10) 
 Stuck with the XI that won 6-0 in Miami and had the game in hand by halftime. Used the second half to give Castañeda and Baker-Whiting their first caps before signing off with another clean sheet.
